interventions.who: cohort criterion; what the labelled series did in this exact situation
interventions.body:
This patient's situation: prior negative biopsy. My criterion answers BIOPSY.

The criterion: repeat, targeted, when the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 4-5 lesion; do not repeat a negative biopsy for an unchanged PI-RADS 3 or lower picture. In the labelled series this criterion matched the reading urologist in 16 of 18 cases in exactly this situation.

Like Expert 1, I have read ONLY the visible panel — not the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the
previous notes or the laboratory panel. Departing from me needs a specific finding from a document
somebody actually opened, named out loud; not a restatement of the panel numbers I already used.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines state that repeat biopsy after a negative systematic biopsy should be considered depending on risk factors such as PSA density and PI-RADS score. "Repeat biopsy after negative biopsy" requires consideration of risk factors such as "PSA density, PI-RADS score."

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert 1's suggestion of biopsy is not decisive because the guideline requires specific risk factors, which the panel variables alone do not establish. Expert 4's focus on the PI-RADS score is relevant, but the guideline indicates that the decision depends on the combination of factors, not just the score.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The guideline requires establishing the PSA density value to determine the risk stratification.
PSA density is 0.14 ng/mL² on the panel, which falls into the 0.15-0.20 ng/mL/cc category according to the retrieved table.
The prior biopsy status is Negative, which is a factor that influences the decision regarding repeat biopsy.
The PSA velocity is 0.97 ng/mL/yr, which is a factor that influences the decision regarding repeat biopsy.
The MRI finding is PI-RADS 5, which is a factor that influences the decision regarding repeat biopsy.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 5.90 ng/mL over 3 points spanning 32 months; velocity +0.94 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 40 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 8.0 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 2.3-28.0.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.74
  uncertainty  +/- 0.10 epistemic (95% band 0.54-0.94), of which 0.00 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents opened by the registrar—the radiology report, PSA trend, and previous notes—directly address the core elements needed to evaluate the open question.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved findings strongly align with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the registrar found a PI-RADS 5 lesion, a rising PSA trend (velocity of 0.97 ng/mL/yr), and a prior negative biopsy status.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. How does the combination of PI-RADS 5, PSA velocity of 0.97 ng/mL/yr, and prior negative biopsy status meet the criteria for repeat biopsy according to the EAU guidelines? The retrieved data establishes the presence of a PI-RADS 5 lesion, a rising PSA velocity, and a prior negative biopsy, which the EAU guideline specialist noted requires consideration of these factors.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 5 score is decisive as it is the primary driver for the cohort criterion that fired the panel protocol. The PSA velocity of 0.97 ng/mL/yr and the prior negative biopsy status are critical risk factors that, when combined with the PI-RADS 5, strongly support the need for further investigation per the EAU framework.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a biopsy based on the strong convergence of high-risk imaging (PI-RADS 5) and concerning serial PSA kinetics following a negative prior biopsy.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
